transition.reason: Implement safe in-app multi-client MCP setup after comparative client research

transition_approval.reference: User instructed: finish the task by following the pyramid workflow, stop asking for approval

intent.statement: Disk Steward users can discover supported local AI clients, explicitly select one or more, and safely set up, verify, repair, or remove the read-only Disk Steward MCP integration without manually editing configuration files or confusing client setup with Agent Access.

success_evidence.description: Settings detects supported installed clients through bounded known signals and lets the user select one or several targets without treating unknown software as supported.
Setup, verification, repair, and removal are idempotent, preserve unrelated client configuration, refuse conflicting ownership, and provide recoverable evidence for every mutation.
The UI distinguishes detection, configuration, client approval, verification, broken configuration, and Agent Access state with accessible text and per-client outcomes.

Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Visual Studio Code, and Claude Desktop receive an honest supported setup path, while other MCP clients receive a copyable manual configuration rather than guessed mutation.
The signed application bundle exposes a stable read-only helper path, and automated tests prove install, upgrade, conflict, verification, removal, and unrelated-setting preservation behavior.

constraints: Preserve native Swift, macOS 13 compatibility, Homebrew and Developer ID distribution, and the bundled disk-witness-mcp helper.
Use official client commands or client-owned installation flows when available; direct configuration editing is a bounded fallback only.
Never require administrator privileges, store client credentials, enable Agent Access implicitly, or add write/delete MCP tools.
Preserve unrelated client configuration and the completed crash-recovery intent and evidence.
Keep detection bounded to known bundle identifiers, executables, and configuration locations; do not search the whole disk.
non_goals: Build a general MCP marketplace or gateway.
Add remote MCP hosting, OAuth brokerage, or credential management.
Redesign monitoring, evidence retention, or cleanup behavior.

assumptions.statement: The distributed non-sandboxed app can invoke installed client CLIs and update user-owned configuration without additional entitlements.
A helper path inside an app installed at a stable Applications location remains valid across normal Homebrew and in-place application updates.

evidence.claim: Disk Steward already ships an executable read-only MCP helper inside the application bundle and exposes Agent Access through a private current-user socket.
The current integration installer is repository-only, directly edits Codex TOML, and writes Claude configuration to a location that is not the current Claude Code user-scope location.
evidence.freshness: Repository and official documentation reviewed on 2026-09-16

evidence.claim: Codex and Claude Code provide official add, list/get, and remove lifecycle commands suitable for app-owned adapters.
Docker MCP Toolkit models multi-client onboarding as explicit connect, disconnect, list, and per-client verification rather than universal implicit mutation.
Cursor and VS Code expose client-owned MCP installation paths, while Claude Desktop provides MCPB packaging with client-managed trust, updates, and auditing.

decisions.question: How should Disk Steward configure several heterogeneous MCP clients?
decisions.choice: Use a typed client-adapter registry with explicit multi-selection, official client-owned commands or flows first, transactional fallback writes, independent per-client results, and a manual configuration escape hatch.
alternatives: Edit every known configuration file directly
Treat setup and Agent Access as one switch
decisions.rationale: The selected path matches mature client-connector practice, preserves client trust boundaries, remains reversible, and keeps Disk Steward's single read-only helper and evidence engine authoritative.

decisions.question: What is the smallest honest delivery ladder?
decisions.choice: First deliver a runnable Codex and Claude Code setup flow in the app, then extend the same lifecycle to Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, and the manual fallback while repeating the first increment's safety checks.
alternatives: One horizontal backend phase followed by UI
Claim client detection alone as an increment
Ship every client without an earlier runnable slice
decisions.rationale: Codex and Claude Code have authoritative CLI lifecycles and are already present in the user's environment, so they form the smallest end-to-end actor-visible setup scenario; the second rung adds heterogeneous client-owned flows and broader regression proof.

nodes.title: Safe multi-client MCP onboarding
nodes.summary: Users can manage Disk Steward's read-only MCP connection across supported local AI clients from one honest, reversible settings experience.

acceptance_criteria.description: All supported-client lifecycle, safety, state-honesty, packaging, and regression evidence passes against the built app.

required_evidence.description: A built application detects representative clients and completes setup, verification, repair, and removal without unrelated mutation.

nodes.title: All supported clients have an honest onboarding path
nodes.summary: The built app extends the verified Codex and Claude Code flow to Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, and manual configuration with per-client lifecycle state.

acceptance_criteria.description: Every named client is detected through bounded signals and receives either a verified adapter or an explicit client-owned/manual handoff.
Codex and Claude Code inherited setup, repair, removal, and Agent Access separation still pass against the final candidate.

required_evidence.description: Cross-client lifecycle matrix and final packaged-app verification.

nodes.title: Codex and Claude Code setup works from Settings
nodes.summary: A user can open Settings, detect Codex and Claude Code, select either or both, set them up, verify their state, repair stale paths, and remove only Disk Steward-owned configuration.

acceptance_criteria.description: The built app completes an end-to-end Codex and Claude Code setup scenario with explicit selection and independently reported results.
Unrelated settings survive setup and removal, conflicts fail closed, and Agent Access remains independently controlled.

required_evidence.description: Swift tests plus a launched settings scenario using fixture client CLIs and configuration roots.

nodes.title: Define the client-adapter and lifecycle contract
nodes.summary: Specify bounded detection, state transitions, command execution, receipts, conflict handling, verification, rollback, and Agent Access separation before product mutations are implemented.

acceptance_criteria.description: The Swift contract represents detected, configured, approval-pending, verified, broken, conflicting, and unavailable states without deriving them from Agent Access.
Mutation operations are explicit, cancellable, independently reported, idempotent, and testable with injected filesystem, workspace, and process boundaries.

required_evidence.description: Unit tests cover state derivation, bounded detection, receipt ownership, conflict refusal, and process failure mapping.

nodes.title: Implement Codex and Claude Code adapters
nodes.summary: Use official client commands for user-scoped add, inspect, verify, repair, and remove operations, with bounded detection and recoverable fallback behavior.

acceptance_criteria.description: Codex setup uses the official shared Codex configuration lifecycle and Claude Code setup uses official user scope rather than the obsolete repository script location.
Repeated setup does not duplicate entries; conflicting entries are not overwritten; removal touches only the owned entry; command and path failures are actionable.

required_evidence.description: Fixture CLI and configuration tests cover detection, setup, repeated setup, verification, repair, conflict, and removal.

non_goals: Cursor, VS Code, or Claude Desktop setup

nodes.title: Build the multi-select Agent Integrations settings experience
nodes.summary: Add a native settings section that rescans known clients, supports multi-selection, executes setup with independent row results, and exposes test, repair, remove, and manual configuration actions.

acceptance_criteria.description: Detected supported clients appear as accessible selectable rows with text status independent of color; absent clients are not preselected.
Set Up Selected reports partial success per client, and setup state remains visually and semantically separate from the Agent Access toggle.

required_evidence.description: Presentation and interaction tests cover scanning, multi-selection, partial failure, repair/remove actions, and accessibility labels.

non_goals: Changing the menu bar status board

nodes.title: Audit the Codex and Claude Code onboarding increment
nodes.summary: Independently exercise the built settings flow, adapter lifecycle, unrelated-setting preservation, conflict refusal, and Agent Access separation.

acceptance_criteria.description: The app builds and a representative multi-select Codex plus Claude Code setup, verify, repair, and removal scenario passes with fixture client homes.
Existing MCP entries and evidence remain unchanged, conflict and unavailable states are honest, and enabling integrations does not enable Agent Access.

required_evidence.description: Build log, focused Swift test output, configuration before/after fixtures, and settings presentation evidence.

nodes.title: Add Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, and manual adapters
nodes.summary: Extend the registry with bounded detection and client-owned installation flows or transactional configuration fallbacks for the remaining named clients.

acceptance_criteria.description: Cursor and VS Code setup delegates trust to their supported installation surfaces where available; Claude Desktop uses a documented supported path; unknown clients receive a copyable stdio configuration only.
Every adapter implements inspect, setup or handoff, verify, repair, and remove semantics honestly, including approval-pending states that Disk Steward cannot complete itself.

required_evidence.description: Fixture tests cover supported client detection, generated configuration, client-owned handoff, conflict behavior, and manual fallback output.

nodes.title: Harden packaging, receipts, repair, and cross-client verification
nodes.summary: Exercise the final built app against stable helper-path, app update, receipt ownership, partial failure, and removal scenarios across all supported clients.

acceptance_criteria.description: The packaged helper path is used consistently and a moved, missing, or replaced helper produces a repairable state rather than silent success.
Receipts permit removal only while the current owned entry still matches; user modifications create a conflict instead of destructive rollback.
A mixed multi-client run reports successes and failures independently and remains safe to repeat.

required_evidence.description: Built-app helper inspection, cross-client lifecycle matrix, and update/repair fixture evidence.

nodes.title: Audit complete multi-client MCP onboarding
nodes.summary: Verify the final candidate across every named client path while repeating the accepted Codex and Claude Code scenario and checking recovery and packaging boundaries.

acceptance_criteria.description: The complete test matrix and application build pass for all supported adapters and the manual fallback.
The earlier Codex and Claude Code multi-select scenario still passes against the final candidate.
No adapter requests administrator access, stores credentials, enables Agent Access, overwrites conflicting configuration, or exposes write/delete MCP tools.

required_evidence.description: Full Swift test output, packaged-app verification, client lifecycle matrix, and safety inspection.
